- A password-reset link is usable for 60 minutes after it is sent, and only once. Requesting a new link retires every earlier unused link of that account, and no other account's. Completing a reset ends every session of that account and nobody else's; afterwards the new password signs in and the old one does not. A request for an unknown address still completes silently, with no link sent. Addresses are matched without regard to letter case.
- Sign-in attempts are limited per account (by address, ignoring letter case), so attempts on one address never lock another account out. A throttled account is refused even with the right password until its limit recovers, and can still request and complete a password reset. Reset requests are limited per address in the same way, independently of sign-in attempts.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.text:
I've fixed all six sign-in and sign-out problems. The existing test suite passes (617 tests), the type-check and lint are clean, and a throwaway check I wrote in /tmp confirmed each expected behaviour before I deleted it.

1. **Signing out signed everyone out.** Sign-out used to run a clean-up that deleted every session created before that moment. It now deletes only the session belonging to that browser. Signing out an unknown or already-ended session does nothing, and a later sign-in starts a new session. The clean-up itself now only removes sessions that have actually expired.
2. **Reset links.** Links were set to expire after 60 seconds instead of 60 minutes; that's corrected. A used link is now refused, and if the same link is submitted twice at once, only one attempt succeeds.
3. **Laptop still signed in after a reset.** Completing a reset now ends every session of that account and no one else's. Afterwards the new password works and the old one doesn't.
4. **Second reset link.** Asking for a new link now retires that account's earlier unused links. Other accounts' links are unaffected.
5. **"Too many attempts" for everybody.**
   - Sign-in attempts and reset requests are now counted per email address, ignoring letter case, and the two limits are separate. The sign-in limit (30 attempts, 10 more allowed per minute) and the reset-request limit (5, 1 more per minute) are unchanged.
   - A throttled account is refused even with the right password until its limit recovers, but it can still request and complete a reset. The reset doesn't clear the sign-in limit early; I read the expected behaviour as asking for that.
   - The final "set new password" step doesn't include an email address, so its limit is counted per link. A shared limit there would let one person block everyone's resets.
6. **"Remember me".** A sign-in without it now lasts 24 hours and one with it lasts 30 days. The login form was already sending the checkbox value; it just wasn't used.

Other changes you should know about:

- **New accounts:** the session created right after registration now uses the 24-hour default rather than 30 days.
- **Email matching:** looking up an address now ignores letter case on the stored address too, not just the typed one.
- **Rate limiter:** it gained an optional fourth argument so a limit can be counted per email address or per link. Existing callers are unaffected.
- **Server actions:** the sign-in and reset actions each had their own site-wide limit on top of the service's. I re-keyed those the same way, so each attempt is still checked twice, just no longer site-wide.

The main changes are in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts`, `session-service.ts`, `session-repository.ts`, `_password-reset-repository.ts` and `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`.
